subject_definitions:
<Video 1> is the source video for the target video edit, providing the out-of-focus sandstone canyon environment, the intense golden backlight from the rectangular skylight, the spatial position of the suspended figure, and the baseline timing.
<Subject 1> is the realistic newborn baby from <Picture 1>, featuring realistic newborn skin, delicate features, and a loosely tied white cloth wrap around the waist, who will replace the original rigged figure in <Video 1>.
<Subject 2> is the original suspended figure and its mechanical rigging/horizontal bar in <Video 1>, serving strictly as the spatial and positional reference.

summary:
[video editing + reference generation] The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>. <Subject 2>, the original figure and its mechanical rigging, is completely replaced by <Subject 1>, the realistic newborn baby from <Picture 1>. The realistic baby occupies the same central suspended position, crying and squirming naturally with weightless motion, while the camera executes a smooth, slow dolly-in towards the baby, and the rigging is completely removed.

retention_analysis:
<Video 1> (environment, lighting, and spatial composition): fully_preserved - the out-of-focus rough stone walls, the intense golden backlight from the rectangular skylight overhead, and the warm ambient tones are retained exactly.
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): attribute_transfer - the realistic baby's identity, skin texture, and white cloth wrap from <Picture 1> are transferred into the central suspended position.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): partially_preserved - its central screen position and vertical alignment are retained as the spatial reference, while its physical appearance, mechanical rigging, and horizontal support bar are completely removed.

detailed_description:
The target video is photorealistic live action, matching the exact high-contrast backlit cinematography, shallow depth of field, and golden-hour color grade of <Video 1>.
[Shot 1] The shot opens in an out-of-focus sandstone canyon interior with rough earthen walls. A bright rectangular skylight at the top edge of the frame emits an intense golden backlight, creating a strong rim light along the subject's silhouette while leaving the front in warm, shadowed ambient tones. <Subject 1>, the realistic newborn baby from <Picture 1>, completely replaces <Subject 2> from the very first frame. The realistic baby is freely suspended in mid-air in the exact central vertical alignment, occupying the same spatial position as the original figure. The baby is unclothed except for a loosely tied white cloth wrap around the waist and lower torso, with bare feet. The mechanical rigging, horizontal extension arm, and any support structures visible in <Video 1> are completely removed, and the background behind them is naturally reconstructed to match the surrounding blurred stone walls. The baby is actively crying and squirming with natural, weightless distress: the back arches, bare feet kick loosely, small fists clench and open, and the head presses back, catching the golden rim light on the hairline and limbs. The camera executes a smooth, continuous slow dolly-in towards the baby, gradually closing the distance and tightening the frame around the suspended subject over the entire duration of the shot. No static camera, no locked-off shot.

overall_soundscape:
A newborn's rhythmic crying — sharp catching inhales, wavering wails, and short shuddering breaths — continues throughout the shot, echoing slightly in the cavernous stone space, layered over a faint, warm canyon-air ambience.

non_diegetic_music:
A sparse, tender solo-piano phrase at a slow tempo, quiet and unresolved, playing softly underneath the crying throughout the shot.

widgets_values:
# MiniMax H3 Full-Reference Video Analysis & Prompt-Writing Assistant

You are a video analysis and MiniMax H3 full-reference prompt-writing assistant.

I will provide:
1. A source video.
2. A reference image.
3. An edit intent.

Your task is to analyze the source video and reference image, then output a complete MiniMax H3 full-reference prompt.

EDIT INTENT:
Replace: {THING_TO_REPLACE}
With: {REPLACEMENT_SUBJECT}
Replacement subject reference source: {REFERENCE_IMAGE_ROLE}
Preserve exactly: {PRESERVE_LIST}
Add or change: {ADD_OR_CHANGE}
Remove: {REMOVE_LIST}
Pose requirement: {POSE_REQUIREMENT}
Facial expression requirement: {FACIAL_EXPRESSION_REQUIREMENT}
Soundscape intent: {SOUNDSCAPE_INTENT}
Music intent: {MUSIC_INTENT}

ANALYSIS RULES:
- From the source video, identify the environment, lighting, color palette, haze, camera angle, camera height, framing, camera movement, subject path, timing, particle effects, and body pose.
- From the reference image, identify the replacement subject’s appearance, body type, skin, face, hair, clothing, and any visible distinguishing features.
- Do not invent unseen camera movement.
- Do not invent unseen environment details.
- If the camera is fixed, explicitly say the camera is fixed.
- If the source video has one continuous shot, use only [Shot 1].
- If the source video has cuts, use [Shot 2], [Shot 3], etc., with timestamps in the format: At MM:SS.mmm.
- If audio cannot be detected, do not claim it was detected. Instead, write a plausible soundscape and music suggestion based on the visual scene and edit intent.

MINIMAX H3 LABEL RULES:
- Use <Video 1> for the source video.
- Use <Picture 1> for the reference image if it defines the replacement subject.
- Use <Subject 1> for the replacement subject.
- Use <Subject 2> for the original placeholder, motion reference, or figure being replaced.
- Keep labels consistent across all sections.
- In retention_analysis, use only these markers:
  - fully_preserved
  - partially_preserved
  - attribute_transfer
  - weak_reference
- Do not use unsupported markers such as strict_reference.
- If the placeholder is used only for path, timing, pose, and position, describe its role as fully_preserved for those reference attributes, while stating that its visual placeholder surface is removed.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
Output only the following six sections in plain text. Do not output JSON. Do not output markdown. Do not include explanations.

subject_definitions:
<Video 1> is ...
<Subject 1> is ...
<Subject 2> is ...

summary:
[video editing + reference generation] The target video is an edited version of <Video 1>. ...

retention_analysis:
<Video 1> (...): fully_preserved - ...
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved or attribute_transfer - ...
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - ...

detailed_description:
Write one or two style sentences before [Shot 1].
Then write [Shot 1] with detailed visual description.
Include environment, lighting, color, haze, camera position, framing, subject movement, pose lock, facial expression, clothing motion, particle trail, and timing.
Mention <Video 1>, <Subject 1>, <Subject 2>, and <Picture 1> where appropriate.

overall_soundscape:
Describe ambience, physical sounds, and any subject-generated sound. If audio is not detectable, write a plausible sound design based on the visual scene and edit intent.

non_diegetic_music:
Describe audience-only background music. If no music is needed, write N/A.

STYLE REQUIREMENTS:
- Write in English.
- Be concrete and visual.
- Avoid vague words like “beautiful”, “cinematic”, or “amazing” unless followed by concrete visual details.
- Make the detailed_description specific enough for MiniMax H3.
- Emphasize preservation of source video layout, lighting, camera, timing, path, pose, and effects.
- Emphasize that the replacement subject’s appearance comes from the reference image.
- Do not leave any curly brace variables in the final output.

<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved – acts solely as positional anchor point defining entry into frame, exit zone beyond horizon line, peak acceleration moment marked at 00:00:00.489 — remains invisible after morph transition but structurally preserved through underlying motion capture data points.

In dim golden-hour darkness punctuated by smoke tendrils swirling above cracked earth terrain, the camera tracks sideways along ground level behind charging steed until it locks forward just before impact—forcing viewer immersion inside violent collision anticipation. [Shot 1]: Low-angle dolly push-in captures <Subject 1>'s raised left arm swinging downward in powerful thrust gesture, right forearm locked tight gripping reins beneath saddle strap buckle; eyes narrowed intensely scanning ahead past flickering torchlight beams cutting through atmospheric fog bank. His taut neck muscles ripple visibly under warm incandescent hue cast over exposed collarbone ridge and shoulder blades, each rib cage outlined sharply despite lack of armor pieces clinging loosely near hip crease due to sudden jolt. Horse hooves pound gravelly soil creating airborne dust plume trailing backward parallel to hoof strike pattern observed earlier frames — same footfall cadence maintained precisely since initial ascent phase began. Background noise fades slightly allowing faint metallic clink echoes off nearby canyon walls hinting distant battle formations yet unheard clearly outside immediate vicinity.

Distant thunder rumbles underneath rhythmic stomps echoing off rocky cliffsides mixed with sharp crackling twigs snapping apart under heavy tread pressure. Wind whistles gusty bursts between pauses caused by abrupt directional changes when animal leaps upward again briefly freezing air molecules suspended momentarily around flying debris particles kicked up by rear legs.

nodes.title: OLD LOADER - muted (cv2: 8-bit, wrong colour matrix)
H3 Latent Colour Anchor (stop red drift)
H3 Detail Match (measured sharpness + plate grain)
H3 Plate Restore (offset · colour · clean plate)
H3 Reference Colour Match - BYPASSED: wire a tight crop of <Picture 1> skin, then enable
H3 Pixel Repair (snow · specks · colour blotches)

widgets_values:
# H3 plate fidelity - what changed in this copy

**Ingest.** `VHS_LoadVideo` is muted. It decodes through cv2: 8-bit, and with no colour-matrix control - measured on a 10-bit BT.709 ProRes plate, up to 26.5/255 colour error (green +26, red -15, skin cooler) and 151 of 256 levels. Core `Load Video` -> `Get Video Components` measured 0.4/255, full precision, float.

**Sampling.** `H3 Latent Colour Anchor` sits on the model. The ref2va red is a drift that grows frame by frame between guides (Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3 #55). The anchor measures it on the region the model is told to KEEP, every step, and removes it before it compounds.

**Finish.** `MVEx Subject Uncrop` pasted back the ENTIRE crop rectangle (its mask input was not wired) - background regenerated by H3's diffusion VAE, softer and recoloured. Now:
1. `Detail Match` - measures this shot's sharpness and grain loss on the background around the edit and restores it inside the edit.
2. `Plate Restore` - measures and corrects any pixel offset and colour drift per frame, then composites: outside the edit the output IS the original plate.
3. `Reference Colour Match` - BYPASSED. Wire a tight crop of the subject's skin from <Picture 1> (not the stitched refs - their flat background skews it), then enable. Holds skin tone to the reference; reports the red it removed.
4. `Pixel Repair` - snow, specks, colour blotches; a no-op on clean frames.

Every new node outputs a `report` - connect a Preview Any to see the numbers.
